0.content:
# agent-sandbox — Fleet, Warm Pool & Isolation

Kubernetes **agent-sandbox** v0.5.2 (`git_commit 9575043`) on cluster `agent-sandbox-demo`, sandboxes running under **gVisor** (`runsc`).

agent-sandbox is the **mirror image of kagent**: it emits **Prometheus metrics + object-watch logs + pod logs, and no traces at all**. Every tile here is metric- or log-derived, never span-derived. Sources: controller `:8080/metrics`, `k8sobjects` CR watch, `kubeletstats`, `filelog`.

All controller-runtime metrics are scoped with `k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo"` — the same tenant also ingests a CAPI management cluster that publishes identically-named `workqueue_*` and `controller_runtime_*` series.

1.content:
## ⭐ Warm-pool efficiency — the headline

A `SandboxWarmPool` exists purely to remove cold-start latency. **Setting `spec.env` (or volume claim templates) on a `SandboxClaim` silently defeats it** — the env changes the effective pod template hash, no pooled sandbox matches, and the claim falls through to a cold create while the pool keeps costing full price.

10.content:
## Controller health

⚠️ **`controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total{controller="sandbox"}` is deliberately not charted as a health signal.** It has a permanent non-zero floor from a benign optimistic-concurrency race (`"the object has been modified"`) that self-heals on requeue. Charting it makes a healthy cluster look broken and alerting on it pages forever. **Use `workqueue_depth` for saturation instead** — it is the honest "is the controller keeping up" signal. The error stream is still shown below, as a triage surface rather than an alert source.

11.description: Backlog per agent-sandbox controller. Sustained depth > 0 means reconciliation is falling behind. This, not reconcile_errors_total, is what to alert on.
11.query: timeseries d = avg(workqueue_depth, default:0), by:{name}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo" and in(name, {"sandbox", "sandboxclaim", "sandboxtemplate", "sandboxwarmpool"})
11.title: Workqueue depth (saturation) — the honest health signal

12.description: 95th percentile of per-interval average reconcile duration (rollup:avg — the Prometheus histogram is ingested as _bucket only, so this is a percentile of averages, not a true bucket quantile).
12.query: timeseries p95 = percentile(controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds, 95, rollup: avg), by:{controller}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo" and in(controller, {"sandbox", "sandboxclaim", "sandboxtemplate", "sandboxwarmpool"})
12.title: Reconcile duration p95 by controller

13.description: How long work sits queued before a worker picks it up. Rising wait with flat depth means worker starvation rather than backlog.
13.query: timeseries q = percentile(workqueue_queue_duration_seconds, 95, rollup: avg), by:{name}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo" and in(name, {"sandbox", "sandboxclaim", "sandboxtemplate", "sandboxwarmpool"})
13.title: Workqueue wait p95 by controller

14.description: Total reconciles in the selected window. The small, persistent 'sandbox / error' bar is the benign resource-version race — expect it to be non-zero on a perfectly healthy cluster.
14.query:
timeseries r = sum(controller_runtime_reconcile_total), by:{controller, result}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo" and in(controller, {"sandbox", "sandboxclaim", "sandboxtemplate", "sandboxwarmpool"})
| fieldsAdd total = arraySum(r)
| filter total > 0
| fields controller, result, total
| sort total desc
14.title: Reconcile throughput by controller and result

15.description: The v1alpha1 <-> v1beta1 conversion webhook. A failing /convert breaks every CRD API call, including kubectl get sandbox. Watch for any code other than 200.
15.query: timeseries w = sum(controller_runtime_webhook_requests_total, default:0), by:{code, webhook}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo"
15.title: Conversion webhook health (/convert)

16.description: Structured error records parsed from controller stdout. Expect a steady trickle of 'Failed to update sandbox status' / 'Reconciler error' carrying 'the object has been modified' — that pair is the benign race, not an incident.
16.query:
fetch logs
| filter k8s.namespace.name == "agent-sandbox-system" and k8s.container.name == "agent-sandbox-controller"
| parse content, "JSON:j"
| fieldsAdd lvl = j[level], msg = j[msg], ctrl = j[controller], err = j[error]
| filter lvl == "error"
| fields timestamp, ctrl, msg, err
| sort timestamp desc
| limit 50
16.title: Controller error log stream (triage, not alerting)

17.content:
## Sandbox resource usage — measured from *outside* the sandbox

⚠️ **`/proc` inside gVisor reports the HOST's memory.** A pod with a 256 Mi limit reads `MemTotal: 12248276 kB` — the node's 12 GiB. Anything that self-reports resources from inside a sandbox (Python `psutil`, Node `os.totalmem()`, JVM ergonomics) is wrong, and a runtime that sizes its heap from `MemTotal` will size for 12 GiB inside a 256 Mi container and get OOM-killed.

These two tiles come from **`kubeletstats` on the node DaemonSet** — outside the sandbox boundary, where the numbers are true. Compare the ~20–25 MiB working set below against the 12 GiB the sandbox believes it has.

*Scoping note:* neither `kubeletstats` nor `k8sattributes` surfaces `runtimeClassName`, and the `agents.x-k8s.io/sandbox-name-hash` pod label appears in series metadata but is not usable as a `timeseries` split dimension. Sandbox pods are therefore scoped by namespace (`default`), which on this cluster contains exactly the sandbox pods.

18.query: timeseries cpu = avg(k8s.pod.cpu.usage), by:{k8s.pod.name}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo" and k8s.namespace.name == "default"
18.title: Sandbox pod CPU (kubeletstats — outside the sandbox)

19.query: timeseries mem = avg(k8s.pod.memory.working_set), by:{k8s.pod.name}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo" and k8s.namespace.name == "default"
19.title: Sandbox pod memory working set (truth, vs the 12 GiB /proc claims)

2.description: warm / (warm + cold) across all claim-owned sandboxes. A pool that is never adopted from reads 0%.
2.query:
timeseries { warm = avg(agent_sandboxes, default:0, filter: launch_type == "warm"), cold = avg(agent_sandboxes, default:0, filter: launch_type == "cold") }, filter: owned_by == "SandboxClaim" and k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo"
| fieldsAdd w = arraySum(warm), c = arraySum(cold)
| fieldsAdd hitRate = if(w + c > 0, 100.0 * w / (w + c), else: 0.0)
| fields hitRate
2.title: Warm-pool hit rate (SandboxClaim)

20.content:
## Sandbox lifecycle stream

**The agent-sandbox controller emits zero Kubernetes Events for its own CRDs** — `kubectl describe sandbox` shows no event history, and Dynatrace's built-in Kubernetes event alerting is blind to sandbox lifecycle. The stream below is the compensating control: a `k8sobjects` receiver in **watch** mode over all four CRDs, with `managedFields` and `last-applied-configuration` stripped (3907 → 1084 bytes, 72% smaller) and the useful fields lifted into flat `agentsandbox.*` attributes so no JSON parsing is needed in DQL.

21.description: Every create, modify and delete of an agent-sandbox custom resource. This is the only sandbox lifecycle history that exists, because the controller publishes no Events.
21.query:
fetch logs
| filter k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo" and isNotNull(agentsandbox.kind) and agentsandbox.kind != "Event"
| fields timestamp, agentsandbox.watch.type, agentsandbox.kind, agentsandbox.namespace, agentsandbox.name, agentsandbox.launch_type, agentsandbox.operating_mode, agentsandbox.ready_status, agentsandbox.ready_reason
| sort timestamp desc
| limit 50
21.title: CR watch stream — Sandbox / SandboxClaim / SandboxTemplate / SandboxWarmPool

3.description: What the sandboxclaim controller actually decided, parsed from its structured JSON stdout. 'BYPASSED (custom config)' is the silent warm-pool killer.
3.query:
fetch logs
| filter k8s.namespace.name == "agent-sandbox-system" and k8s.container.name == "agent-sandbox-controller"
| parse content, "JSON:j"
| fieldsAdd msg = j[msg]
| filter in(msg, {"Successfully adopted sandbox from warm pool", "Bypassing warm pool adoption because custom configuration is provided (env or volume claim templates)", "creating sandbox from template"})
| fieldsAdd decision = if(msg == "Successfully adopted sandbox from warm pool", "WARM HIT", else: if(msg == "Bypassing warm pool adoption because custom configuration is provided (env or volume claim templates)", "BYPASSED (custom config)", else: "COLD CREATE"))
| summarize c = count(), by:{decision}
| sort c desc
3.title: Warm-pool decision breakdown

4.description: cold vs warm over time for SandboxClaim-owned sandboxes. A flat line at cold with zero warm is the failure mode.
4.query: timeseries sb = avg(agent_sandboxes, default:0), by:{launch_type}, filter: owned_by == "SandboxClaim" and k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo"
4.title: Claim-owned sandboxes by launch type

5.description: The proof tile. Each SandboxClaim and the decision the controller logged for it. Claims carrying spec.env appear as 'Bypassing warm pool adoption'; the env-free claim adopts a pooled sandbox.
5.query:
fetch logs
| filter k8s.namespace.name == "agent-sandbox-system" and k8s.container.name == "agent-sandbox-controller"
| parse content, "JSON:j"
| fieldsAdd msg = j[msg], claim = j[name], ns = j[namespace]
| filter msg == "Bypassing warm pool adoption because custom configuration is provided (env or volume claim templates)" or msg == "Successfully adopted sandbox from warm pool"
| fieldsAdd verdict = if(msg == "Successfully adopted sandbox from warm pool", "WARM HIT", else: "BYPASSED — custom config (spec.env / volumeClaimTemplates)")
| fields timestamp, ns, claim, verdict
| sort timestamp desc
| limit 50
5.title: Per-claim warm-pool verdict (which claim got bypassed, and why)

6.content:
## Fleet inventory

`agent_sandboxes` is a point-in-time gauge whose label set encodes *how* each sandbox came to exist. Cardinality is bounded and safe (48 combinations per namespace × template) — no dimensional-explosion risk.

7.description: The whole fleet: who owns each sandbox (None = hand-written, SandboxWarmPool = pooled member, SandboxClaim = claim-bound) and how it started.
7.query: timeseries sb = avg(agent_sandboxes, default:0), by:{owned_by, launch_type, sandbox_template}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo"
7.title: Sandbox inventory by owner and launch type

8.description: Mirrors Sandbox.status.conditions[Ready]. A sustained ready_condition=false series is the alertable signal; a brief blip is a normal cold start or a suspend.
8.query: timeseries sb = avg(agent_sandboxes, default:0), by:{ready_condition}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo"
8.title: Readiness — not-ready sandboxes

9.description: expired=true means the sandbox is past spec.shutdownTime. Anything non-zero here for long is a garbage-collection leak — you are paying for sandboxes that should be gone.
9.query: timeseries sb = avg(agent_sandboxes, default:0), by:{expired}, filter: k8s.cluster.name == "agent-sandbox-demo"
9.title: Expired but still alive (reclamation leak)
